span.p:
One state, two scopes.
gate_scope = contact → human gate G2, first outbound
email, enforced by policy P1
gate_scope = decision → human gate G1, risk acceptance
Gates are what a person does; policies are what the
chokepoint enforces. Both tokens are signed, single-use
and scoped, and both are verified at the gateway with a
PUBLIC key — never in the user interface, and never with
a key the gateway could sign with.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Enterable from any state.
Parks the review with a dashboard card
explaining what stalled and why.
It never silently corrects.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
History is never mutated.
A reopened review is a new record
linked to the old one, so the
audit trail stays intact.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Re-tiering is the one legitimate backward
move inside a single review. Tier only ever
goes UP — a downward re-tier is an attack
surface. Every change increments plan_version
and writes a TierChange naming the evidence.
